newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway energy minister quits over spy scandal.
newsitem.headline: Norway energy minister quits over spy scandal.

text.p: Norwegian oil and energy minister Grete Faremo is resigning in a scandal over the national intelligence service's surveillance work, Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland announced on Monday.

He told parliament he had accepted the resignation of Faremo, who was justice minister at the time of the scandal in June 1995 involving the surveillance of a member of a government-appointed committee assigned to examine the work of the intelligence service.

The scandal broke last week when it was learned that the intelligence service sought information last year from the former East German Stasi security policy files on investigator Berge Furre, a former left-wing politician.
The commission he belongs to has studied the Cold War surveillance of communists in Norway by the intelligence service.

Jagland told parliament: "Minister Faremo has today told me that she takes the constitutional responsibility for the ministry's handling of the surveillance of Berge Furre. She has today submitted her resignation. I have accepted it."
The national news agency NTB said Hans Olav Oestgaard, head of the intelligence service, was also stepping down for his role in the scandal.
